newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures end down on weak demand.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures end down on weak demand.

text.p: Rubber futures closed lower on Monday as buyers stayed away from the market after engaging in shortcovering last week to cover their requirements for the month, dealers said.

"It's terrible. The buyers stocked up last week. China's bought everything it needed. The buyers have the upper hand now. The difference between the buying and selling price is so wide. Buyers can really pick and choose," a local rubber trader said.
Another dealer said the market languished in the absence of action in nearby or forward months. "This is a very bad day. We did nothing," one dealer said.
"It's a stagnant market. This is just the first working day of the month and it does not look good," another trader said.

Only 275 tonnes of the January RSS3 contract was sold in the local exchange. There were no other trades done here, dealers said. At around 0945 GMT, January RSS3 was seen at 124.75 U.S. cents a kg from Friday's settlement of 125.00 cents a kg.
January RSS1 was indicated at 177.50-179.50 Singapore cents (US$1.27-$1.28) a kg from the previous 179.50 cents.
January TSR20 was indicated at 172.00-174.00 Singapore cents (US$1.23-$1.24) a kg from 174.50 cents.
